rationale: Evidence from the baseline (iteration 0, no race yet, development sim only): all 60 trials went off track on oval, s-bend and slalom, with 1 line-loss event each and progress of only 0.04 to 0.12. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m, and the measured max_error is about 0.061 m, so the robot drifts just past the allowed band right after losing the line once. rms_error (about 0.03 m) is low, so the robot is tracking reasonably until a transient pushes it out. Likely causes: (1) the outer sensors at x = +/-0.04 with 12 mm footprints barely see the 25 mm tape until the error is about 0.02 m, so the line is lost too early on bends; (2) base_speed 1.6 is too fast for the bend and recovery transients; (3) kp = 2 with a +/-2 signal gives up to about +/-4 turn, which is aggressive for a line-follower with weak sensing. Changes: (a) sensors spread to x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, +0.015, +0.03 with 16 mm footprints, so the outer sensors overlap the tape at about 0.0045 m error and line loss needs error above about 0.058 m; (b) kp reduced from 2.0 to 1.5 and kd raised from 0.05 to 0.1 to damp the response; (c) base_speed reduced from 1.6 to 1.4 to give the bends more margin, and line_loss kept as last_direction. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, max_error below 0.06 m on the development tracks, and some completions. The cost is a slower lap (about 3 s at 1.4). Hypotheses to check next: if completion is 1 with time above 2.8 s, raise base_speed toward 1.6 to 1.7; if max_error still exceeds 0.06 on the s-bend, reduce base_speed further or increase kd.
